02Services

Four trades.
Traditional
materials.

Every job starts with the same question. What was this wall built with, and how was it meant to behave?

01/ 04 · Discipline

Stonemasonry

Banker masonry and fixing. We draw templates, carve stone from the block and lay it in traditional lime mortars and grouts, from a carved tracery window to a limestone rubble wall.

View stonemasonry

02/ 04 · Discipline

Plaster
& render

Lime plaster, render, cornices, mouldings and ceiling roses, repaired or run from scratch to match the original. We are one of the few WA contractors with deep experience in lath and plaster ceilings and walls.

View plaster & render

03/ 04 · Discipline

Tuckpointing
& repointing

We cut out fretting joints and old cement pointing, then repoint in lime matched to the original profile, texture and colour. Brick, stone, tuck and chimney pointing.

View pointing

04/ 04 · Discipline

Conservation
& restoration

We keep original fabric wherever possible and replace it only when there is no alternative. Preservation, restoration, rehabilitation or reconstruction, chosen to suit the building.

View conservation
Specialist treatments
05Salt attack & rising damp

We find the source of the moisture first. Then, if it’s needed, a chemical damp course or new damp-proof course, and a poultice system that draws damaging salts out of the wall.

06Crack stitching

Stainless steel stitching bars grouted across the crack to reconnect and strengthen the masonry, once a structural engineer has confirmed the cause.

07Cleaning & paint removal

Low-pressure, high-heat water cleaning to bring limestone and brick back to life. No harsh chemicals, which speed up the decay of soft masonry.

08Roof cleaning & repairs

Professional cleaning, tile replacement and repointing on heritage roofs.

Also: brickwork restoration · chimney repairs · stone replacement · render mouldings · lime renders for new buildings

03Lime, not cement

Cement traps water. Lime lets a wall breathe.

Most walls built before 1919 were designed to let moisture escape as water and vapour. Hard cement pointing and non-breathable paint seal it in, so the softer brick and stone around them decay first.

  1. 01Find the source of the moisture before treating anything.
  2. 02Remove cement mortar and render that is damaging soft masonry.
  3. 03Repoint and render in lime, matched to the original.
Lime mortar vs cement mortar
04Selected work

Selected
work.

Gold rush courthouses, a port weighbridge and an 1871 homestead, from Fremantle to the Goldfields.

01 / FeaturedFremantle · 2019

Weighbridge Station

Built 1921 · State Heritage Register · Rebedding and full lime repointing

Coastal weather had fretted the original lime mortar and later cement repairs made it worse. We removed all cement and repointed the building in a lime mortar selected by the City of Fremantle.

View project

02 / FeaturedKalgoorlie · 2018

Exchange Hotel

Built 1900 · State Heritage Register · Cellar desalination, lime render

A poultice system drew damaging salts out of the soft stone cellar walls. A lime render now keeps drawing salts out and slows the stone’s decay.

View project

03 / FeaturedPeppermint Grove · 2019

Peppermint Grove

Private residence · Donnybrook sandstone · Hand-carved doorways and cornicing

Carved from the block in local Donnybrook sandstone to match the original house, then fixed using traditional stonemasonry.
